Numerous locally heavy showers and isolated to scattered
thunderstorms continue to build tonight as the outer rainbands of 
Bavi move in, and conditions will continue to deteriorate hereafter. 
Gusty north winds of 15 to 25 mph will gradually increase across the 
islands tonight, then rapidly increase tomorrow afternoon as tropical
storm conditions, including sustained winds of 39 mph or more, begin
to move into the coastal waters. Typhoon force winds of 74 mph or 
greater are expected from early Monday morning to early Monday 
afternoon, with peak, potentially super typhoon conditions forecast 
to arrive late in the morning to around noon. The southern Marianas, 
including Guam and Rota, can generally expect winds to shift west to 
southwest during passage, while Tinian and Saipan may see north to 
north-northwest winds rapidly shift east, then south to southeast as
the storm passes. This narrow time range and wind shifts are highly 
dependent on Bavi's eventual arrival time and location of its 
passage, and uncertainty exists. After typhoon conditions pass, 
strong southerly tropical storm winds (58 to 73 mph) will continue 
through the late afternoon to early evening Monday. Then, winds are 
expected to fall below tropical storm conditions during the early 
morning hours of Tuesday. See the Tropical Systems section below for 
more details on Super Typhoon Bavi.

Marine...
Combined seas of 5 to 8 feet and moderate to fresh northerly winds 
will continue to build tonight as Super Typhoon Bavi approaches the 
Marianas from the east. Heavier rain bands and thunderstorms from 
Bavi will increase across Marianas coastal waters overnight and 
conditions will continue to deteriorate. Tropical storm conditions 
are expected to arrive to the Marianas starting late Sunday afternoon
or Sunday evening. Super Typhoon Bavi is expected to move through 
the southern Marianas Monday morning with the forecast track 
currently near or just north of Rota. Seas will build significantly 
over the next 24 to 36 hours, as Bavi-induced wind waves and 
localized storm surge develop on approach. Seas will quickly rise to 
between 25 and 35 feet ahead of and during the passage of Bavi late 
Sunday through Monday, with seas up to 45 feet possible near the 
center. Winds, showers and seas will begin to subside once Bavi 
begins exiting to the west-northwest by Tuesday night. 

Tropical Systems...
Bavi (09W) was upgraded to a Category 5 super typhoon this morning 
at 0700 ChST, and it continues to maintain a westward track towards 
the Marianas. STY Bavi is currently located about 390 miles east of 
Guam near 12.6N 150.5E, and it is moving west at around 8 mph. Bavi 
remains a very dangerous, well-organized storm, and it is expected to
maintain Category 5 strength through Monday as it makes passage 
through the Marianas. Tropical storm force winds are expected to 
begin as early as late Sunday afternoon or Sunday evening. Then, 
Typhoon conditions will begin to be felt Monday morning as Bavi 
crosses the islands, and are expected to depart Monday afternoon. The
latest forecast track maintains Bavi's passage somewhere over the 
southern Marianas, near or just north of Rota, but there is time for 
the track to shift north or south. All islands will experience 
impacts. At minimum, damaging tropical storm force conditions are 
expected, but damage will be catastrophic near the center of Super 
Typhoon Bavi. Maximum sustained winds are currently forecast at 170 
mph at time of passage, with gusts to 200 mph possible. Regardless of
the exact forecast track, Bavi's center could potentially pass over 
any point between Guam and Saipan. 

Intense, torrential rainfall will accompany the passage of Super 
Typhoon Bavi, capable of producing significant flooding and 
mudslides. Surf will become extremely dangerous ahead of Bavi's 
approach, potentially reaching 30 feet Monday, with the greatest 
increase initially felt along north and east facing reefs, followed 
shortly thereafter by west and south facing reefs. Significant 
coastal inundation and erosion are expected, with inundation levels 
potentially reaching 10 to 15 feet nearest the storm's center 
passage.

For more information on Super Typhoon Bavi, please refer to the 
Tropical Cyclone Public Advisory issued by the National Weather 
Service under WMO header WTPQ31 PGUM and the Tropical Cyclone Warning
issued by the Joint Typhoon Warning Center under WMO header WTPN31 
PGTW.

Eastern Micronesia...
Wet weather will continue through tonight at Pohnpei as convergent
southwest flow continues to promote numerous showers and isolated 
thunderstorms across portions of Pohnpei State. Conditions will begin
to improve on Sunday with only isolated to scattered showers and 
isolated thunderstorms expected through much of the upcoming week.
